substrates.name: FR-4
substrates.notes: Standard PCB, not suitable for high-frequency RF. Properties vary significantly with manufacturer, resin content, and frequency.

substrates.name: Rogers RO4003C
substrates.notes: Hydrocarbon ceramic laminate. Drop-in replacement for FR-4 in RF applications. Compatible with FR-4 processing. Stable epsilon vs frequency and temperature.

substrates.name: Rogers RO4350B
substrates.notes: UL 94V-0 flame retardant hydrocarbon ceramic. Popular for commercial RF. Compatible with standard FR-4 fabrication processes.

substrates.name: Rogers RT/duroid 5880
substrates.notes: PTFE glass microfiber reinforced. Very low loss, excellent for microwave and mm-wave. Low epsilon reduces surface wave excitation on patch antennas.

substrates.name: Rogers RT/duroid 6002
substrates.notes: PTFE ceramic filled. Low loss and isotropic. Preferred for space and defense phased arrays. Excellent dimensional stability.

substrates.name: Rogers TMM 10i
substrates.notes: Thermoset ceramic-loaded plastic. High dielectric constant enables compact antenna designs. Isotropic and dimensionally stable.

substrates.name: Isola IS680
substrates.notes: Low-loss PTFE/hydrocarbon blend. Halogen-free, lead-free compatible. Good alternative to Rogers for cost-sensitive RF applications.

substrates.name: Taconic TLY-5
substrates.notes: Woven PTFE/fiberglass. Similar performance to RT/duroid 5880. Woven reinforcement improves dimensional stability vs non-woven PTFE.

substrates.name: LTCC (DuPont 951)
substrates.notes: Low Temperature Co-fired Ceramic. Multi-layer hermetic packaging. Silver or gold conductors co-fired. Used for SiP, embedded passives, and mm-wave modules.

substrates.name: Alumina 96%
substrates.notes: 96% purity aluminum oxide ceramic. Thick-film and thin-film metallization. Used for hybrid microwave integrated circuits (MICs) and chip packages.

substrates.name: Alumina 99.5%
substrates.notes: High-purity alumina. Extremely low loss. Used for precision microwave filters, resonators, and mm-wave substrates.

substrates.name: GaAs
substrates.notes: Gallium arsenide semi-insulating substrate. MMIC fabrication with integrated active devices. Excellent for mm-wave and sub-THz applications.

substrates.name: Silicon (High Resistivity)
substrates.notes: High-resistivity silicon (>1 kohm-cm). RFIC and MEMS substrates. tan_d varies significantly with resistivity; HR-Si (>10 kohm-cm) achieves tan_d < 0.001.

substrates.name: Quartz (Fused Silica)
substrates.notes: Amorphous SiO2. Extremely low loss and stable epsilon. Used for precision mm-wave filters, MEMS substrates, and optical-frequency components.
